method: Freeze the current stereo regression and lower-band response. As a separate bounded nomination, take 120 ms segments every 80 ms from the same four residual frequency bands. Nominate future offsets when at least two bands agree by mean-centered normalized correlation of at least 0.62. At the nomination stage only, use every second band sample. Keep up to two peaks per segment separated by 128 samples at 8 kHz, aggregate by votes and then peak score, and test each of the best 12 coarse lags and the 16 kHz neighbors within two samples with the unchanged final band and interval rules. The existing prediction has priority; the local arm enters only when the baseline has an assessed recording but no pair. No earlier copy, labels, timing prior or learned weights enter scoring.
calibration: Use four excerpts each from the already source-verified DLIVING and OOFFICE recordings, with independent AMI material ES2004a and TS3004a. The gain and alignment thresholds of the existing check and the new nominations are fixed. Verify numeric coverage and no extra ordinary highlights in this development split before any held run. The exact receipt must be published beside the held readout.
held: Use six disjoint excerpts each from the source-verified DKITCHEN, NFIELD, STRAFFIC and TMETRO recordings at 39, 69, 126, 158, 233 and 288 seconds. Exclude any time overlap with the original short PCM/Opus AAC transfer and the playback-speed trials on these rooms. New foregrounds for this comparison come from the separate ES2011b and IS1006b AMI meetings. Underlying recordings have prior exposure in other tasks. Measure the same staged repeat at both speech-above-room levels and six controls for each source group. Controls are original room recordings, ordinary panned speech, a different room excerpt, a moving foreground position, repeated foreground speech, and identical channels. Report 192 distributions per carrier, with every delivered case linked to its exact parent and clocks.
carrier: Opus qualification remains exact, mono and ordinary-reference behavior untouched. Opus is a single stereo 3.75-second 48 kHz Ogg stream with 188 20 ms 400-byte packets, 312 leading and 168 trailing samples removed, and exactly 180000 presented samples confirmed in independently decoded native stereo frames. Compare 160 kb/s AAC on the identical WAV parent. Preserve all half-open sample coordinates without interpolating endpoints.
acceptance: An improved experimental Opus method must add at least three correct pairs across two source groups and allow at most two new ordinary highlights and two new misplaced edited cases. Each pair requires 0.50 intersection over union on both intervals. Adoption also requires at least 16 useful pairs of 48, across at least two held rooms and both speech-to-room ratios, and at least 85% retention of paired matched AAC successes. Clock failures are separate from model errors. Interpret the evidence as repeated sound with zero weight in AI confidence.
